met_analysis:
The Deep Depression over Southeast & adjoining Southwest Bay of Bengal moved north-northwestwards with the speed of 10 kmph during past 06 hours, intensified into a cyclonic storm “Akvan” [Pronunciation :Akvan]” and lies centered at 1730 hours IST of today, the 16th November, 2026 over central parts of South and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal, near Latitude 12.2°N and Longitude 85.7°E, about 610 km east of Chennai (Tamil Nadu), 630 km northeast of Trincomalee (Sri Lanka), 660 km southeast of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 670 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 790 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha). It is very likely to continue to move north-northwestwards and intensify further into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal around evening of 17th November, 2026. Thereafter, it is likely to move northwestwards and intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm around 19th November morning. Continuing to move northwestwards, it is likely to cross Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni, around noon of 20th November, 2026 as a very severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 kmph.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Northeast Assam & neighbourhood extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Sikkim & neighbourhood extending upto 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Southeast Arabian Sea & adjoining north Kerala coast at 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over south Konkan & neighbourhoodat 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
